look: XORA site look, same as the V00 welcome film: deep void ground, frosted glass panels with thin cyan-to-violet edges, fictional market lines drawing in, calm eased motion, the brain tutor guiding from the bottom-right corner

scenes.name: Lesson thirteen
scenes.desc: Title card: Phase 3, lesson T13, Liquidation, Funding and Futures Risks; a margin-buffer ring drains while a funding clock ticks; the tutor walks in.

scenes.name: Closed for you
scenes.desc: Educational mock: a 10x long's margin balance sinks and the position card flips from Open to Closed by the exchange.

scenes.name: Your margin buffer
scenes.desc: Margin balance = margin + unrealized PnL: 10x long, 100 USDT margin, 1,000 notional; BTC falls 1%, 3%, 5% and the buffer shrinks to 90, 70, 50 toward an unnumbered maintenance level.

scenes.name: Liquidation
scenes.desc: Liquidation defined as forced closure when the margin balance reaches the maintenance level; the bar touches the line and the position is stamped closed; conceptual, not an exchange formula.

scenes.name: Leverage and room
scenes.desc: Same 1,000 USDT position at 10x (100 margin) and 4x (250 margin); a 5% fall costs 50 USDT in both, leaving 50 of 100 versus 200 of 250; more room is not safety.

scenes.name: Mark price
scenes.desc: Mark price defined; a one-off spike in the last price barely moves the smoother mark price line; liquidation checks usually use mark price.

scenes.name: Funding
scenes.desc: Funding rate defined for perpetual futures; a clock reaches the funding time and 0.10 USDT flows from longs to shorts (1,000 x 0.01%); the arrow flips for a negative rate.

scenes.name: Funding adds up
scenes.desc: Nine funding times over three days: 0.90 USDT at 1,000 notional, 9 USDT at 10,000; it comes out of the margin balance.

scenes.name: Gap risk
scenes.desc: A stop at 59,000; news makes price jump from 59,600 straight to 58,300; the stop triggers but fills near 58,300.

scenes.name: Common mistake
scenes.desc: Misconception: a stop-loss protects from liquidation. A high-leverage position's liquidation zone sits above a far stop; price reaches liquidation first. A stop-loss is not liquidation insurance.

scenes.name: Try it
scenes.desc: Scenario: wild swings before news, small buffer, unsure. Choices: add leverage, hold and hope, reduce or close and wait. Countdown; answer C.

scenes.name: Know the risks
scenes.desc: Liquidation, funding, gaps and slippage, no guaranteed safe strategy; reduce exposure or NO_TRADE when unsure.

scenes.name: Recap
scenes.desc: Three key points and a check question: a stop-loss cannot guarantee you will not be liquidated.

scenes.name: Up next
scenes.desc: End card: Phase 3 complete; next, Checkpoint A, reviewing T01 to T13.
